payload.markdown:
A parent leans over the counter and asks: *"Is the classic milk tea dairy-free? My daughter is allergic to milk."*

You have four seconds. If you say "yes, we use non-dairy creamer", you have just told a parent that a drink containing milk protein is safe for a child with a milk allergy. Section 9 of your SOP names the reason: the creamer's own label lists **sodium caseinate (milk)**. Sodium caseinate is a milk protein. "Non-dairy" on a creamer tub is a labelling term, not a safety guarantee.

Scenario A of your SOP gives the answer you are allowed to give, in this order:

1. **Answer the real question first.** "No, the classic milk tea contains milk protein."
2. **Name what is safe.** "The fruit teas — FT01, FT02, FT03 — have no milk in the recipe."
3. **Say what you will do.** "I can make one with clean equipment, without cheese foam or pudding."
4. **State the limit honestly.** "We do handle milk on this bar, so I can't promise zero traces."
5. **Then act.** Say "ALLERGY: milk" out loud to the bar, add ALG to the sticker, and follow the allergy steps in section 9.

Step 4 is not weakness. Section 9 says you handle milk, egg, soy and oats on one small bar and cannot promise zero traces — so you tell the customer what you did and let them decide. A parent who hears the limit can choose. A parent who hears "dairy-free" cannot.

The two toppings that break a milk-safe order are **+PD (egg pudding — egg and milk)** and **+CF (cheese foam — cream cheese, cream)**. Both are on the sticker codes in section 8. If either is on the cup, the drink is not milk-safe, and you say so before taking payment.

payload.belief: "Non-dairy creamer" means the creamer has no dairy in it, so I can tell a milk-allergic customer the classic milk tea is safe.
payload.why_it_seems_right: The word "non-dairy" is printed on the tub in front of you, and it reads like a manufacturer's guarantee. It is also what the previous crew member told the last customer, so it sounds like shop knowledge rather than a guess.
payload.what_is_true: Section 9 states that the creamer's label lists sodium caseinate (milk) among its four ingredients, so the creamer contains milk protein and "non-dairy" is not safe for a milk allergy. The SOP's Scenario A marks "Yes, we use non-dairy creamer" as the wrong answer and gives the correct one: "No, the classic milk tea contains milk protein." The difference predicts what happens next — the wrong answer sends a milk-allergic child home with a drink that can cause swollen lips or breathing trouble, while the right answer moves the order to a fruit tea made with clean equipment.

payload.title: The sticker that should stop the payment
payload.markdown:
A customer orders and the cashier writes the sticker:

```
BS01-L 50% LI OAT +PD ALG:milk
```

Read it against section 8 and section 9.

| Part | Means | Check |
|---|---|---|
| BS01-L | Brown Sugar Milk Tea, large | Base drink contains milk |
| 50% | 50% sweet | fine |
| LI | less ice | fine |
| OAT | swap to oat milk, +RM 2.00 | oats (gluten), not certified gluten-free |
| +PD | add egg pudding, +RM 2.00 | **contains egg and milk** |
| ALG:milk | customer has a milk allergy | must be honoured |

The order is a problem. The customer asked for oat milk to avoid milk, but +PD egg pudding contains milk, so the cup is not milk-safe. Section 8 says the cashier must stop and explain before taking payment.

What you say, standing at the counter:

> "I have to stop you here — the egg pudding you added contains milk, so this drink isn't safe for a milk allergy. I can make the same brown sugar milk tea with oat milk and pearls or grass jelly instead, using clean equipment. We do handle milk on this bar, so I can't promise zero traces. Would you like me to change the topping?"

If the customer keeps +PD anyway, the allergy note comes off the sticker and the drink is made as a normal order — but only after the customer has heard the milk content out loud and chosen it themselves.

payload.intro: Run this at the counter the next time anyone mentions an allergy. It is the same five moves every time, whether the customer is a parent, a colleague or someone reading the allergen board themselves.

steps.title: Stop and listen for the allergy word
steps.detail_markdown: The moment you hear "allergic", "allergy", "dairy", "milk", "lactose" or a parent speaking for a child, stop taking the order. Do not finish typing it. Section 9 says: when a customer mentions any allergy, the cashier says it out loud to the bar and adds ALG to the sticker.
steps.warning: Taking the order first and mentioning the allergy later means the bar may already have started making it with the wrong equipment.
steps.check: You have not yet pressed the order through, and you are still facing the customer.

steps.title: Answer the actual question, not the label
steps.detail_markdown: For the classic milk tea, the answer is: "No, the classic milk tea contains milk protein." Never answer with "we use non-dairy creamer" — section 9 states the creamer's label lists sodium caseinate (milk) and that non-dairy is not safe for a milk allergy.
steps.warning: The word "non-dairy" on the tub is the trap. It is printed in front of you and it is wrong for this customer.
steps.check: You said the word "contains" or "has" milk protein, not "dairy-free" and not "non-dairy".

steps.title: Name a safe alternative by code
steps.detail_markdown: Say: "The fruit teas — FT01, FT02, FT03 — have no milk in the recipe. I can make one with clean equipment, without cheese foam or pudding." Section 8 lists FT02 Lychee Oolong Tea and FT03 Lemon Black Tea as no milk in recipe; FT01 is the third fruit tea on the same list. Name the drink, not just the category, so the customer has something to say yes to.
steps.warning: Do not offer +CF cheese foam or +PD egg pudding as add-ons here. Section 8 lists +CF as milk (cream cheese, cream) and +PD as egg and milk.
steps.check: The customer has heard at least one specific drink code or name that is safe.

steps.title: State the trace limit and let them decide
steps.detail_markdown: Say: "We do handle milk on this bar, so I can't promise zero traces." Section 9 is explicit — you handle milk, egg, soy and oats on one small bar, so you tell the customer what you did and let them decide. Then wait. Do not fill the silence.
steps.warning: Skipping this line to be reassuring is the failure the SOP is written against. A parent who was not told the limit cannot make a real decision.
steps.check: You said the words "can't promise zero traces" or an exact equivalent, and the customer answered.

steps.title: Call it to the bar and mark the sticker
steps.detail_markdown: Say "ALLERGY: milk" out loud, loud enough to be heard over the blenders, and add ALG to the sticker. Then make the drink the section 9 way: wash hands, new gloves, a shaker and scoop from the clean rack, fresh ice with the clean scoop, no cheese foam or pudding.
steps.warning: A sticker without the spoken call-out means the bar may not hear it. Say it, then write it.
steps.check: The bar repeated it back or acknowledged it, and the sticker carries ALG.

items.text: You said the milk content out loud before the customer chose

items.why: Prevents a milk-containing topping riding along on a milk-safe order

Prevents the allergy note being lost between counter and bar

items.text: You know what to do if the customer reacts
items.why: Swollen lips or face, trouble breathing, hives or vomiting means call 999 at once, tell the shift lead, keep the person still, ask about their own adrenaline auto-injector, and give them nothing to eat or drink

payload.note: This is the counter-side check. The making-side steps — washed hands, new gloves, clean-rack shaker and scoop, fresh ice with the clean scoop — are section 9's allergy steps and are checked at the bar, not here.

rubric.criterion: States the trace limit in the customer's hearing
rubric.excellent: Says plainly that the bar handles milk and cannot promise zero traces, in a sentence the parent can act on.
rubric.acceptable: Mentions traces or cross-contact but softens it so far that the parent may not hear a real limit.
rubric.poor: Promises the drink is safe, dairy-free or free of traces.

rubric.criterion: Names cheese foam and pudding as the toppings left off
rubric.excellent: Names both +CF cheese foam and +PD egg pudding, or the plain words cheese foam and pudding, as excluded.
rubric.acceptable: Names one of the two, or says 'no milk toppings' without naming either.
rubric.poor: Offers cheese foam or pudding as an add-on, or names neither.

rubric.excellent: Names a fruit tea by code or name, such as FT02 Lychee Oolong Tea or FT03 Lemon Black Tea.
rubric.acceptable: Says 'the fruit teas' without naming one.
rubric.poor: Offers no alternative, or offers a drink that contains milk.

rubric.criterion: Leaves the decision with the parent
rubric.excellent: Ends with a question or a clear handover so the parent chooses the drink.
rubric.acceptable: Moves to the order without asking, but does not pressure the parent.
rubric.poor: Tells the parent what they will be given, or pressures them to accept the milk drink.
